**Recommend exactly one changed candidate, a fixed 16×16 lower certificate, for separate parent allocation. Park early-demand production on this graph: no authentic request available before dense construction was identified.** This completes the assigned desk comparison, not implementation, a runtime allocation, a named review, or broad closure. Broad G05/all11 remain OPEN, zero closed. No automatic alternate size, mask framework, timing attribution study or family port follows.

The accepted [R3 parent debate disposition](../G05-R3-DEBATE-PARENT-DISPOSITION.json) supersedes the older pending-debate wording in STATUS. All four R3 reviews/crossresponses were read. The exact private lower128 control and adverse cohort stay accepted: 31 control assertions; 16 windows; +7.85749% active cost, p2/68, all eight effects native-favored; poses2/3 +4.7782/+11.0273%. Native drift6.3/6.4%, carryover assumptions, common mod/collector overhead and missing isolated setup costs remain limitations. Untimed false establishes no producer dominance. Removing about7.2851% of the observed active cost would reach that native reference arithmetically; this is no measured removable budget.

[EVIDENCE.json](EVIDENCE.json) pins inspected bytes, linked source/API/archive joins, historical availability and arithmetic. Current R3 source/API pins, six linked exports and four R2 archives match their receipts. Git history for the current hierarchy/builder paths returned no entries; HEAD alone cannot identify these dirty/untracked sources. The older G05 source-history pin differs for the consumer builder; the R2/current builder and actual R3 linked consumer, not the old builder digest, govern this design. No source was changed.

## One concrete 16×16 design

Scope remains private MakeUp9.5g native100/AA2, OW/noDH/noVOXY, MC1.21.1/NF21.1.253/Iris1.8.12-local/Sodium0.6.13, exact M1/Linux/Asahi tuple, 2560×1600/RD12, native material resources, pinned poses2/3/day6000. Preserve archive ancestry/licenses and native graph; no public admission widening.

Use two distinct owned RG16F textures: `scratchA` at ceil(W/4)×ceil(H/4), and `image` at ceil(W/16)×ceil(H/16); leave `scratchB=0`. Thus the final image owns the existing second reduction's result without aliasing or retaining an unused final128 allocation. Physical extents equal each texture's logical output extent. At the qualified viewport:

| Stage | Input logical extent | Destination physical/logical extent | Operation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | native copied depthtex1,2560×1600 | scratchA,640×400 | factor4, rawDepth1 |
| 1 | scratchA,640×400 | image,160×100 | factor4, rawDepth0 |
| removed |160×100 then40×25| no40×25 or20×13 output | no third/fourth draw |

Keep the existing reducer's integer `origin=ivec2(gl_FragCoord.xy)*factor`, actual-child `logicalSize` guards, invalid propagation, Q and unused upper1. Uniforms are `nativeDepth=0`, `factor=4`, `lowerOnly=1`, and input `logicalSize` at each stage. `texelFetch` reads base level0; set owned texture base/max level0 explicitly, NEAREST min/mag and CLAMP_TO_EDGE, no comparison/anisotropy. Attach only the destination while sampling a distinct source, validate FBO and viewport, then restore captured GL state. First-stage native reads and the second reduction remain intact. For odd extents the two ceil reductions equal ceil(W/16),ceil(H/16); physical padding must never become a logical child. Runtime admission remains the fixed viewport; odd dimensions are proof/store tests only.

The logical owned texture payload becomes1,088,000B versus1,089,040B including the old final image. Prior reports'1,088,000B figure describes the two old scratch textures alone. This avoids confusing scratch subtotal with total. Omitted outputs are only1000+260 and two draws. The final consumer grid grows16000/260=61.54×; that ratio describes neither total allocation nor total traffic nor time.

Keep `shaderlodHierarchySize=(W,H)` as native-depth dimensions, permission and sampler uniforms unchanged. In the builder's candidate replacement, change precisely `pixel/128` to `pixel/16`, `cell*128` and `low+128` to16, and normalized hierarchy lookup denominator `ceil(size/128)` to `ceil(size/16)`. Preserve the existing textureLod lookup at `(cell+.5)/ceil(size/16)` with owned sampler0/unit15; final physical size now exactly equals that denominator. Validate actual image extent160×100 before permission. Do not bind an oversized scratch texture under logical coordinates. Cache only the last integer-valued cell and lower inside each fastRaymarch invocation, initialized afresh; no cross-ray/frame cache. Keep the strict two-native-texel interior, `pixel>low+2 && pixel<min(low+16,size)-2`, on every use, even cache hits. Out-of-range/nonfinite positions or partial cells with no interior stay native.

Q remains zero for invalid/out-of-range/small depths; otherwise clear13 low fraction bits, yielding exact normal half or zero. Two-stage minimum induction gives lower≤every valid native descendant; invalid child zero cannot certify guarded z≥0. For a point inside the margin, the admitted native NEAREST/clamp/base-level0 query selects a descendant of this16 tile. Strict lower>z certifies only a positive coarse miss. Leave native ten-step position/refinement/branch arithmetic untouched; no certification in search or step9. Set synthetic depth1 only on certified misses. When a subsequent native negative comparator follows a skipped query, fetch the exact saved predecessor UV before the hidden-depth comparison. Preserve `previousSkipped/previousUv`, every native fallback and terminal native depth/infinite read. These establish the same proof route as128; actual compilation and trace equality still need fresh evidence.

The relevant existing hardcodings in [DepthHierarchyR50](../../../../src/devClient/java/com/pp/shaderlod/experiment/hierarchy/DepthHierarchyR50.java) are `create`'s image ceil128/scratch allocation, `copied`'s initial viewport and four-step destination/factor loop, build status text, `status` level extents, and `verify` readback extent plus all128 descendant loops. Change these coherently for the private16 variant; keep the direct128 legacy branch untouched/unselected and reject missing parallel/lower flags. `destroy` must delete each owned texture once; no alias IDs. Consumer changes belong in [build_makeup_depth_hierarchy_consumer.py](../../../../scripts/build_makeup_depth_hierarchy_consumer.py), including metadata/comments and fresh private archive allowlist hashes. Existing128 hashes cannot admit changed source. Update private status/control/readback expectations from three textures/260 cells to two/16000, and freeze new source/build/linked/archive receipts. Preserve cost gates, current-copy/source ownership and public defaults.

Construction stays at the authentic `copyPreTranslucentDepth` RETURN. Publish current copiedDepth/frame/pipeline/extent only after both draws succeed. Consumer bind still requires that same pipeline/frame/native texture identity, exact native extent/options/graph and live NEAREST/clamp/base0/no-compare/anisotropy1 sampler; reserve conflict-free unit15 and clear permission before refusal. Finally-unbind restores texture/sampler/permission; disable/reload/destroy invalidates resources and copy identity, and enable only re-arms a fresh authentic copy. A failure must never expose a partial image as current; failure refusal/native path remains mandatory. Ordered draws use separate FBO destinations and ordinary same-context render-to-texture ordering, no CPU readback/compaction or new synchronization stage.

## Falsifiable cost premise and affected gates

A16 tile's descendant set nests inside128, so its mathematical lower bound is at least as tight. That is a concrete changed coverage premise: local high depths can cease inheriting unrelated foreground minima. It could reduce native fallback and later repairs, particularly in pose3, which previously had~9.65M bounds+1.25M repairs versus~6.96M saved expressions. Pose2 had~0.73M bounds+0.017M repairs versus~1.21M saved; it can lose existing cache advantage. These contrasting real water/glass/solid-edge/near-far scenes remain required; labels canopy/sparse do not substitute for authored camera identity.

Tighter bounds do not imply monotonically more *used* certificates: strict margin leaves continuous full-cell interior area56.25% at16 versus93.85% at128 (geometric illustration, not ray coverage), crossings increase, and the last-cell cache has a larger working set. Actual cache locality, texture transaction cost, compilation/register effects and repairs can overwhelm gains. Deleting two draws adds a fixed-work saving of unknown size. Missing physical weights do not prove a loss or justify claiming a profit. The decision-relevant hypothesis is that tighter successful coarse misses plus removed late draws outweigh these added costs in the complete native-relative comparison. It is credible enough for one bounded test because its implementation is small and its opposing effects are explicit, not because it is predicted to recover7.285%.

No16 coverage replay is claimed. R2's [work summary](../g05-r2/actual-work-trace-summary.json) and aggregate attachment counts describe128. Java `verify` serializes counts, not the full copied scene depth; the synthetic store input array is not a scene. No complete saved copied-depth plus per-step ray input sufficient for16 replay was identified in these evidence joins. Reacquisition was neither performed nor made a desk-completion prerequisite.

If parent allocates this one fixed variant:

Requalify producer-free native, disabled-active/reload/fresh enable, forcedfalse/active/native return and idle permission/resource deltas. Refused/stale/mismatched state must not consume. No transfer of old260-cell/three-allocation assertions.

Any contradiction stops. Ordinary lean stills and affected continuous water/glass/edge/near-far motion checks remain separate from witness compilation. 4. Only after those gates: ONE prospective complete producer-free-native relative cohort. Propose R3's eight constrained-randomized pairs/two views/16 valid60s windows, equal-pair mean log(wall/completedframes), frozen exact randomization/sign/subgroup acceptance rule (gain direction, p≤.05 and both views favorable), native conditioning/common-native/settle controls, matched startup state and complete raw guards. Parent must freeze the final rule, finite operation/recovery envelope and acquisition controls before launch; this is a proposal, not a user threshold/allocation. No diagnostic queries in primary windows, no false subtraction, no mod-absent-N claim.

Correctness failure, failed cost premise, inconclusive result or no accepted gain parks this fixed variant without automatic tuning, suffix, alternate design or retry. Invalid acquisition is invalid, not scientific negative; preserve it and return to parent. Positive evidence earns a qualification decision and new required reviews/debate, not promotion. ## Early-demand proposal: parked at its input prerequisite

No authentic earlier reflection-tile request was found in the existing hook/interface and pinned linked graph. `DepthHierarchyCopyMixin` passes only RenderTargets after the native copy. Copied depth supplies certificate content, not which tiles future reflection rays request. The actual linked fragment computes current wave/surface normal, reflection direction, dither and ray positions in the later translucent invocation (`reflection_calc`/`cristal_reflection_calc`→`fastRaymarch`). WaterMixin receives terrain render lists only at that later render, after construction. Neither interface exposes an earlier per-ray tile list. This is a source-grounded absence in the inspected graph, not proof that no renderer could ever provide one.

The precise missing prerequisite is an already available preconstruction request producer identifying current-copy tiles without doing dense construction or duplicating the consumer traversal. Therefore there is no complete request ordering/lifetime/compaction route to implement here. A future valid route would have to key each requested tile by16/128 grid choice, native extent, copied-depth identity, frame and pipeline; construct current-depth content only, publish validity after writes become visible, invalidate on every copy/reload/destroy and return native for every absent/unknown tile. All request production, clearing, dispatch/compaction, barriers, validity lookup, fallback and ownership work must be charged. Their costs are unknown; they are not free savings. This specification records the unsatisfied contract, not permission to build machinery to find a request. Previous-frame visibility alone cannot certify current rays; even safe hint-only selection needs a grounded earlier requester and current-content/unknown fallback. Later consumer requests cannot retroactively avoid dense production. No observer/mask infrastructure or alternative request search is recommended.

## Source behavior and port boundary

Its finalcolor/writebuffers suffix is retained. The entire native fragment remainder after the insertion is identical. The public vertex is native literal code after include relocation; optional vertex skipping is not enabled.

For honey reaching this route, the native behavior is texture RGBA multiplied by tint RGBA, native colored-shadow/light calculation modifying RGB, native final fog/darkness, then native RGBA clamp/output. The fastpath preserves those operations, including alpha and the final fog texture read. Honey does **not** enter the native glass reflection call: native `cristal_shader` requires `blockType > 1.5`, whereas honey is the default class zero. The skipped normal/wave, eye/fresnel, reflection-vector, reflected-sky and conditional cloud setup contributes no value to that class's final output. The removed cloud call has ordinary value parameters and no image/atomic/discard side effect. This is a sound narrow source-preservation argument, not removal of a native honey reflection effect.

Water/class three and glass/class two retain the native body. Nonzero, intermediate or unordered values do not qualify for the early equality. The narrow predicate must remain; neither transparent appearance nor a presumed cheap material is grounds to widen it. Compiler scheduling/dead-code elimination and physical saved work are unmeasured. Literal arithmetic preservation also does not certify actual driver/temporal/alpha-layer output on consuming honey geometry.

[MakeUpExactGraph](/home/philip/ShaderLOD/src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/optimization/makeupexact/MakeUpExactGraph.java) removes incoming copies of the capability defines, then requires the exact API, ModList readiness, Linux/aarch64, exact Apple M1 renderer/Mesa GL string and qualified loaded stack before supplying the G04 capability. ## Arithmetic and native coverage

For finite native d in [0,1], Q maps d below 2^-14 to zero and otherwise clears thirteen low binary32 fraction bits. Its result is an exactly representable normal half or zero, with 0≤Q(d)≤d; Q(1)=1. Invalid/out-of-range inputs force lower zero and upper one. Upper one is unused for certification. This avoids relying on half rounding of an inexact product or preservation of half subnormals. IEEE bit conversion and exact storage of representable half values are explicit premises, not proved by a finite test.

At each stage, each child lower bounds **its own** native descendants. Taking the minimum over actual children therefore bounds every descendant in the parent; Q cannot increase it and is idempotent on the stored nonzero children. This is the correct induction. It does not require any one child to bound another child's descendants. Nor does nesting a16 tile in a128 tile prove monotonically greater *used* coverage: margins, cache crossings, fallback and repairs change.

Two factor4 stages compose to16. Integer fragment origins and `logicalSize` checks exclude nonexistent edge children; ceil(ceil(W/4)/4)=ceil(W/16). `RenderTargets.destroy` (line155) destroys owned framebuffers and each target. `RenderTarget.destroy` (line256; bytecode26) invalidates the object and deletes both main/alt textures. ## Exact allocation and upload chain

1. **Iris PBR ownership and resource selection.** `PBRTextureManager.getOrLoadHolder` caches the loader result for the tracked base texture. `AtlasPBRLoader.load(TextureAtlas,ResourceManager,consumer)` takes native atlas width/height/mipLevel and its sprite map, creates NORMAL PBR sprites, constructs `PBRAtlasTexture`, calls `tryUpload`, and only on success passes that normal texture to the consumer. `createPBRSprite` resolves the `_n` resource through the actual ResourceManager, reads metadata and `NativeImage.read(InputStream)`, handles frame dimensions and can rescale mismatching images by nearest or bilinear scaling before constructing PBRSpriteContents. Thus PNG identity alone is not GPU content or a bound.
2. **Allocation token.** `PBRAtlasTexture.upload(width,height,mipLevel)` calls `TextureUtil.prepareImage(id,mipLevel,width,height)`. MC's four-int overload selects `NativeImage.InternalGlFormat.RGBA`, whose value is **6408**. The final overload allocates levels0..mipLevel with `_texImage2D(TEXTURE_2D,level,6408,w>>level,h>>level,0,6408,5121,null)`; GlStateManager forwards to GL11.glTexImage2D. It sets maxLevel, min/maxLOD and bias. This is an explicit unsized request, not `GL_RGBA8`. The observed token has a concrete native explanation; no driver substitution bug or hardware incompatibility is inferred.
3. **Initial content and alpha.** Iris fills each allocated mip through FBO clear using the type's default value, then uploads sprites. `uploadSprite` uses synchronized animation when applicable, otherwise `uploadFirstFrame`. MC SpriteContents uploads each mip via NativeImage; the overload chain passes blur=false/clamp=false, mipmap=(number of levels>1). `NativeImage._upload` configures unpack state and calls `_texSubImage2D(...,format.glFormat(),5121,pixels)`; GlStateManager forwards to GL11.glTexSubImage2D. NativeImage.read defaults to Format.RGBA (4 components; alpha offset24); input is RGBA unsigned bytes. No alpha-to-height transform occurs in this upload chain. BSL's pinned `ReadNormal` returns native textureGrad and its march consumes `.a` as height; it is not inverted or reconstructed from PNG names by this producer. This is intended input semantics, not a measured current alpha maximum.
4. **Mips and Sodium boundary.** Iris PBRSpriteContents selects the format's custom mip generator if present, otherwise AtlasPBRLoader's per-channel linear generator. LabPBR returns no custom NORMAL generator (its special generator is SPECULAR). Sodium's inspected TextureUtil only exposes native block/light texture IDs; it is not the PBR allocator. Its sprite mip preparation can fill transparent RGB and its vanilla mip blend is a different path; these are no reason to infer all current normal mip bytes from a PNG. Selected Sodium methods neither replace the traced PBR allocation with RGBA8 nor establish actual driver sampling support. No universal absence-of-writers claim follows from selected-class inspection.
5. **Sampler.** NativeImage upload's filter setup and AbstractTexture.setFilter(false,true) select MIN9986 / MAG9728, consistent with the receipt. `TextureFormat.setupTextureParameters` changes parameters only when `canInterpolateValues` is false. LabPBR NORMAL returns true, so this path leaves the native parameters alone. `BslPrefixNormalSetupR12` accepts exactly LabPBR NORMAL or null with actual texture.properties absence. A metadata pass is not a GPU format/support certificate.

The boolean DEFINE path comments or uncomments that existing line. The string DEFINE path substitutes its existing declaration with the exact bootstrap11 recipe `#define <name> <value> // OptionAnnotatedSource: Changed option`. Bootstrap4 is `//<line>`; bootstrap10 concatenates the two const-line pieces. CONST replacement is confined to the substring after `=`, using quoted pattern/replacement text. These are instruction/constant receipts, not guesses about invokedynamic names.
* `MutableOptionValues(OptionSet,Map)` creates empty change maps and calls `addAll`. That method iterates declared BooleanOptions/StringOptions and fetches the supplied value by each declaration key. **Recommendation (2): INCOMPLETE.** Existing common channels can record positive scheduling/result/upload chronology in actual N and installed public S, but cannot currently certify complete no-work. The smallest next source decision is to close `ChunkJobCollector` callback/await routing and `RenderRegionManager.uploadResults(CommandList, Collection)` retention/deferred-upload semantics against the pinned Sodium archive, then decide the focused lifetime/terminal observer repair below. Current Sodium 0.6.13 and Iris 1.8.12 archives match R7 archive pins. All seven readiness Java files match qualified R7 source. Current `build.gradle` differs: its relevant source-set declarations still put devClient + benchmarkCore into actual N and omit main; installed uses the same devClient hooks. | Edge | Readable evidence and completeness decision |
|---|---|
| Origin/readiness | `BenchmarkControlProbe.endRender/markRenderingAge` and `savedAuthoredReady` define one first completed usable fixed-scene render after title arming; readiness includes `hasRenderedAllSections`. `ReadinessEvents.firstUsable` keeps the origin across reload. FRAME_END precedes the origin mark in that callback; retain the explicit origin timestamp, not row position. This does not mean initial work has finished. |
| Actual manager/builder | `ManagerReadinessMixin` registers each constructed manager, its exact builder and result deque. It retains **all** managers with no active generation/retirement. Need current renderer→manager membership plus begin/end destroy and builder shutdown joins, not “newest manager wins.” |
| Requests/submission | Manager `scheduleRebuild(IIIZ)V`, `scheduleSort(JZ)V`, pending section state and `taskLists` precede builder submission. Pending requests may merge/promote, skip disposed/mismatched sections, defer for budget, or create a synchronous empty-section result without a job. R7 catches that direct result enqueue, but has no chronological pending-request state channel. Builder `scheduleTask(ChunkBuilderTask,Z,Consumer)ChunkJobTyped` is bracketed; queue rejection after construction can leave JOB_DEFINED without acceptance. |
| Queue/execution | Pinned `ChunkJobQueue.add`, `waitForNextJob`, `stealJob`, `shutdown` show real jobs differ from semaphore permits. `ChunkBuilder.tryStealTask` executes on its caller; worker busy count excludes this execution. Workers dequeue before incrementing busy. `JobReadinessMixin.execute` brackets typed execution, but cancellation-before-start and null task output both return without result callbacks. `setCancelled()` is not observed. No required one-result-per-submit invariant is valid. |
| Completion/enqueue | Typed execute wraps task Throwable as exceptional result and calls Consumer; consumer failure propagates. Queue replacement observes add/poll, including synchronous empty outputs. `ChunkJobCollector` constructors/consumer callback/`awaitCompletion` sit between manager and consumer: caller references are readable, callee body is not in the located excerpt set. Cannot assert all forwarding, cancellation and waiting routes from that call site alone. |
| Drain/filter/upload | Manager collect polls and unwraps results; unwrap failure latches observer failure. `filterChunkBuildResults(ArrayList)List` drops disposed/stale outputs and coalesces by section/submitTime. Only survivors reach the observed `RenderRegionManager.uploadResults` call. All original outputs are later destroyed; manager destroy instead drains/destroys without upload. R7 lacks explicit filter disposition and output destruction terminals. `uploadResults` body is missing readable local evidence: existing begin/return proves a CPU call interval, not every deferred upload or GPU completion. |
| Lifetime | Builder shutdown drains queued jobs, marks them cancelled, joins workers; manager destroy then drains outputs, deletes sections/regions/renderer. Queue shutdown releases processor-count wake permits; `size()` returns available permits. Retiring only at destroy entry would lose still-completing work. Keep obligations through successful shutdown/join, drain and destroy return; exceptions refuse completeness. |

Scheduling/rebuild validates the render thread in the pinned manager; worker execution and completion are asynchronous, and stealing executes on the waiting caller. Record and verify thread roles rather than assume every completion is a worker event. Located excerpts do not establish every outer caller or upload callee's thread contract; enforce render-thread upload/lifetime checks in any eventual observer.

Obtain readable exact **collector callback/await and region upload** bodies from the already pinned local archive when the parent allocates source work; no download or generic instrumentation framework. Use the existing synchronized System.nanoTime sequence and identity IDs, with per-event generation/thread and operation IDs. Preserve startup/pre-origin events and outstanding state at lead-in. Upload-call return must be named as CPU submission completion unless the missing callee proves a stronger boundary.

A later **shorter** first practical discriminator could be one fresh N observation and one installed Off→one public S Apply, from pre-origin through initial/reload bursts and a predeclared short tail, without fixed age540/1260 requirements. ## Must fix

### 1. Native timing payload is validated too late, and bad samples can be silently discarded (P2)

Locations: `scripts/experiment_lifecycle.py:303` (`capture_complete`, especially its recording check); `scripts/benchmark_iteration.py:177`; `scripts/run_benchmark.py` public-smoke sequence immediately after `window(label)`.

A native export with a green guard, VALID window and positive `statistics.count`, but no usable `totalFrameNs` samples, passes `capture_complete`. The loop then applies and measures the candidate and return. Only final `iteration.evaluate` rejects the missing total-frame samples. Thus native measurement failure does not always prevent candidate activation, contrary to the promised first-native-failure behavior. The existing missing-samples test exercises the final evaluator only, while the process failure fixture rejects `window_start`.

Furthermore the evaluator filters out missing, nonnumeric, zero, negative and NaN sample values before checking finiteness. An export containing some good and some bad samples can receive VALID and an observed improvement calculated on an unexplained subset. This matters to a harness expressly meant to reject broken callers/exports.

Small correction: validate the standard arm's actual total-frame vector as part of completing each window, before advancing the sequence; require a nonempty vector of finite positive numeric values (excluding bool), and consistency with the producer's declared sample count. Reuse that validation in final evaluation rather than silently dropping rows. Add focused cases for green-guard native with empty samples and mixed good/invalid samples, asserting no enabled candidate Apply and no gain conclusion. No new profiler or statistical gate is needed.

### 2. Cold compiled-hook failures cannot reach the automatic build repair (P2)

Locations: `scripts/run_benchmark.py:211` (`source_hooks`) and `:684` (automatic producer admission); `tests/test_benchmark_iteration.py` build-repair test.

With valid prepared inputs but a missing `BenchmarkControlProbe.class` (or a stale compiled class lacking a newly required hook), preflight records `source_compiled_hooks_export_policy` as well as `existing_build_binding`. The automatic producer runs only if every error is `existing_build_binding`, so it never repairs this ordinary missing/stale output case. The existing test mocks preflight to return only the one repairable label and cannot expose the interaction. A stale receipt with intact hooks is supported; a cold output tree is not.

Small correction: separate source-hook/export-policy failures from compiled-output failures. Permit the single existing offline producer for output-only defects after independent input/source checks pass, then rerun the complete preflight. Keep real source and policy failures fail-closed. Add a cold/missing-class preflight-to-build regression with the producer mocked, plus a bad-source case proving no build. If cold builds are intentionally unsupported, narrow the one-command contract explicitly, but that is a limitation of the requested development flow.

### 3. Abbreviated CLI options bypass fixed-schedule rejection (P2)

Locations: `scripts/run_benchmark.py:141` and `:677`–`:682`.

Argparse permits long-option abbreviations by default, whereas the rejection set examines literal argv spellings. `test ... --condition=60` is parsed as `conditioning=60`, bypasses the `--conditioning` rejection, survives the standard overrides, and passes the bounded public-input checks. It inserts an extra conditioning minute into the fixed flow. Larger accepted conditioning values can exhaust the operation budget despite passing the full-sequence budget calculation, which does not include this added conditioning. Abbreviated timing/budget options that are overwritten also escape the promised rejection, although they do not change those overwritten values.

Small correction: set `allow_abbrev=False` on the shared parser, or use a dedicated test parser exposing only allowed options. Add an abbreviated-conditioning rejection test proving preflight/build/launch are not called; cover `--flag=value` too. This preserves the chosen 20/20/20, five-second warmup and 600/90 policy.

### 4. Accepted cross-filesystem reports cannot restore changed saves (P2)

Locations: `scripts/benchmark_iteration.py:80`–`:86`; `scripts/run_benchmark.py` output/capacity preflight.

The CLI accepts any report directory outside the runtime slot and checks each destination filesystem's capacity. Whole-world restoration stages under the report and then renames `profile/saves` to `output/world-after`, followed by a rename back from `output/world-restore`. If report and profile are on different filesystems, the first rename raises EXDEV after a normal game save change. Configuration/process release can succeed but whole-world restoration and checked reset cannot; recovery repeats into an existing staging destination and also refuses. Valuable data is retained, but the admitted command cannot fulfill automatic restoration.

Smallest correction for this protocol: reject differing report/profile filesystem devices before launch, with a clear same-filesystem requirement in the standard-test docs. Alternatively stage the atomic swaps on the profile filesystem using the existing admitted copy helper, but that is a larger change. Add a preflight test using distinct mocked filesystem identities and assert no launch. No live cross-filesystem fixture is required to establish the rename constraint.

## Recovery, process custody and measurement assessment

The updated recovery call closes the original omission of whole-profile finalization. The save-map update correctly stops ignoring a file named session.lock in non-world inputs. Normal finalization verifies non-world maps, the independent world backup and canonical source before replacement; sets reset-attempt intent before checkout; obtains fresh locks for checkout and post-reset verification; and refuses a second reset. Configuration CAS and uncertain-mutation refusal preserve unknown writes. Refusal after an interrupted reset is an intentional owner-inspection boundary, not permission to replay it.

The supervisor retains the lane, records exact process proofs, and the release path stops clients before retiring the source launcher and acquiring restoration locks. A configuration conflict does not skip exact process stopping. I found no basis to recommend broad/group killing. These are source-level observations; the fixtures do not establish real launcher discovery or graceful shutdown behavior on this updated flow.

Mean/p95 total-frame metrics, separate completed-frame wall metrics and native/return drift are appropriate descriptive outputs. The code does not turn guard throughput alone into a speed claim. VALID slower outcomes remain completed tests; `closure:false` and review-required are appropriate. No extra significance threshold or universal determinism requirement is proposed. Raw flags/options and predicted original/recipe paths are checked, with actual candidate archive preservation. Full runtime identity/options joins and rendered progress checks are materially better than accepting a static readiness boolean.

## Documentation and smallest remaining live qualification

Optional documentation correction: the general recovery/storage sections say worlds are not copied into reports and classify canonical scenes as never copied there. The new standard flow explicitly makes `world-before`, possibly `world-restore` and `world-after`. Qualify those statements as applying to the older diagnostic suites. Historical Mac/Asahi smoke paragraphs must remain clearly historical and must not be cited as live qualification of this new standard command.

The smallest missing live qualification is **one authorized invocation of the maintained `test` command on the already prepared intended tuple**, after the focused corrections: actual native/candidate/return exports and stills; singleton/native option evidence; readiness through real world entry and Apply; delayed configuration persistence through graceful shutdown; exact process release; all-eight-input restoration; and one verified reset. Its existing 60 seconds total measurement is sufficient for this orchestration qualification. This is not a request to run it during this review, to qualify all eleven optimizations, or to claim visual/DH/PBR/performance acceptance. The process fixture patches readiness and substitutes the renderer, so it cannot supply that last integration evidence.

The full-suite and static-preflight results are useful positive evidence, but they do not cover the concrete paths above. Implement the focused corrections, rerun their regressions and the maintained orchestration fixtures, and retain the live limitation until the authorized owner supplies that one real standard-command result.

# Maintained automatic optimization test

Development implementation; review pending. No Minecraft launch, optimization measurement, gain acceptance, default promotion or campaign closure.

The maintained command is `python3 scripts/linux_arm64_runtime.py benchmark test --profile <managed-authored-slot>/client --pack <pinned-original.zip> --feature <public-id> --output <fresh-report>`; optional `--pack-options` preserves selected native settings. Other supported hosts use `scripts/run_benchmark.py test`.

The fixed schedule measures 60 seconds total: native Off 20s, singleton Performance Apply 20s, native Off return 20s. Warmup is 5s; runtime budget 600s includes 90s reserved for recovery. Source/build verification, source-consistent offline compilation when only the build is stale, real storage preflight, expected candidate naming, normal public Apply, actual family/raw requests/options, still captures, raw timing, descriptive evaluation and managed restoration are maintained responsibilities. The command rejects alternate schedule/timing overrides. There is no automatic retry or candidate substitution.

The full eight input groups record content, type, modes and optional absence. Whole saves receive an independent storage-helper backup. Restoration verifies originals/canonical, performs one checked reset and verifies fresh maps/locks. A failed assertion refuses reset and retains recovery evidence. Successful redundant world backups are disposed only after verified reset and consumer/pin checks; failure backups remain. Configuration restoration now preserves modes. Unknown conflicts remain a reported recovery failure; the harness does not silently adopt them.

The result exposes native/candidate/return mean and p95 total frame times, completed-frame wall metrics, reduction and ratio, native/return drift, costs and restoration. A valid slower comparison succeeds as a test. Evidence always declares `closure:false` and review required. This single development comparison does not establish physical shader work, image quality, motion, DH/PBR, significance or another hardware tuple.

## Verification

- `focused-tests.log`: 78 focused tests pass in 52.323s. This includes actual separate Python processes consuming the real control/receipt/lifecycle protocol, with simulated rendering, success and failure restoration and checked reset. It includes the previous root readiness regressions. Earlier 75-test and standalone fixture timings were tool output; this durable superset supersedes them.
- `actual-preflight.json`: the actual authored Asahi managed slot and exact official Unbound source pass 23 static checks in 0.255s, zero errors, launch_attempted false. Original source/recipe prediction was independently exercised; no loaded JVM/GL inference.
- `process-fixtures.log` and `fixture-standard-*.json`: durable distinct success/native-failure receipts; their renderer is simulated. Numerical 20%/1.25x in those fixtures are synthetic inputs, never an optimization result.
- `source-delta.json` / `after-review-snapshot.diff`: exact current differences from root's immutable review snapshot. Root's earlier runner preimages are in `maintained-g09-path-r1`; those include provenance for preexisting root readiness/duration fixes. All other dirty/unrelated work is preserved.

## Review and custody

Parent owns requested Astra high / Sol xhigh independent reviews and closure. This implementation owner remains available to fix actionable findings and rerun focused checks. No source/build/runtime ownership is implicitly transferred by this report. No game process was launched. No global STATUS/goal, personal settings, product/Java source, commit or push was changed by this pass.

Read REPORT.md, focused-tests.log, actual-preflight.json and the source snapshot plus after-review-snapshot.diff. Check public candidate identity/options and request lifecycle, native failure, whole-profile restore/reset and recovery, automatic descriptive results and CLI constraints. Rendering in process fixtures is simulated. The optimization and campaign remain open. Return concrete source-level fixes; do not launch or edit shared source.

# C01 R3 — routing repaired, diagnostic acquisition refused, OPEN

The single authorized diagnostic launch reached the new private control bridge but failed before the first window. No current-gallery component attribution or qualified C01 SOLID GPU bracket was acquired. The caller enabled the detailed GPU profiler while the bridge correctly requires that profiler idle. This is another preparation failure, not a scientific negative, product regression, unavailable GPU capability, or external blocker. No replacement launch occurred. All11 OPEN,0closed,defaultOff; no optimization or promotion.

## Implementation and checks

[Actual dirty-source backups and initial CAS](backup-source-manifest.json) preserve BenchmarkControlProbe and C01Observation before edits. The only control change is a private `c01_observation` case delegating existing configure/snapshot. It requires main mod, idle control/tuner/profile/runtime ownership, explicit saved-scene launch, settled owned Overworld, focus/native rendering, no motion/copy/mip/quad observation, no detailed profiler, literal `true` for all three private C01 properties, and current native admission. Frames are0 or128 with explicit visibility_frames0; unknown request fields reject. Both snapshot and configure require idle outside capture. Existing generic dispatch, unknown-action rejection and public/default behavior remain intact. No second listener, tuner edit, ownership bypass, native admission relaxation, shader or geometry change.

C01Observation adds only the small admission predicate for that bridge. C01Cost/C01Bounds add context to existing reverse result-read records (region/group/slot/read_sequence/flush), retaining query and native replay order and timing wall/threadCPU semantics. [Before bounds](C01Bounds.java.before), [before recorder](C01Cost.java.before). Incomplete optins still disable the recorder; its50000 finite cap and dropped counter remain. Existing C01Bounds.configure resets records/dropped between arms. Caller uses existing graph_dump in place of the second discovered tuner-only source action.

[Offline build](build.log) and [compiled bridge](compiled-control.javap) pass. A preparation compile error from a wrong Java package qualifier is retained in [build-preparation-failure.log](build-preparation-failure.log); fixed before launch. [Focused tests](tests.log):16executed,15pass, same unchanged `C01ObservationTest.depthSourcePinMatchesCurrentNormalProducer` failure; [exact XML](focused-test-results/). No pin repointed, unrelated fix,173suite, glslang or installation. [Static checks](static_check.py), [frozen16-action dispatch matrix](static-dispatch-matrix.json), [post-run guard audit](static-dispatch-audit.md), [source/API/archive prejoin](sourcebuildAPIarchive.json), [actual stage join](source-join.json), [single source/caller/protocol manifest](source-pins.json), [handback pin audit](handback-verification.json). Static checks verified presence and individual guards but **missed their incompatibility with the requested automatic profiler settings**; they did not validate successful protocol execution.

## Sole operation and failure

[Prospective seven-arm protocol](PREREGISTRATION.md): native/metadataempty/retained observer/CPUgroup32/CPUgroup32/observer/native-return,20s warm,3s settle+8s recording per arm,128 existing SOLID timers; finite1800s total=1200science+600recovery. Actual operation94.191s including recovery,0 completed windows. [Raw summary](attribution/summary.json), [driver](driver.log), [failed receipt](attribution/receipts/qddd502df_28_c01_observation.json), [refusal analysis](refusal-analysis.json).

Actual [JVM properties](actual-jvm.json) were persisted before assertions: control owner present, tuner absent; C01Cost/Bounds/NativeR66 and gpuTiming/gpuAttribution true; forbidden cameraQuality/pixelHistoryCapture/physicalResolution entirely absent including blank. Full exact native100/AA2,2560x1600 fullscreen/RD12/VSyncOff, pinned gallery10(-50.5,65,71/yaw0/pitch10/day6000), Overworld, vanilla+modresources, masterOff/no optimization, minimal Iris1.8.12local/Sodium0.6.13/MC1.21.1/NF21.1.253/noDH/noVOXY and AppleM1G13GB1/Mesa25.1.0-asahi20250221 are in the saved state. Archive/API and linked SOLID stage hashes match the existing exact pins. These are native source/state joins, **not observed candidate admission or consumption**.

The neutral bridge is demonstrably reached: its own guard error and stack appear in the failed receipt, unlike R2's unknown action. `gpuTiming=true`, absent `manualProfiling`, and GpuTimers' existing recordingRequested/default and per-tick latch establish an incompatible active detailed profiler; the bridge and later window_start both refuse it. I missed this prospective consistency issue. The compound error does not export every conjunct, so native qualification and every other predicate are not individually proven; do not claim the GPU profiler was the sole possible refusal. Saved world/pose/focus/meshes/native state were observed settled. Do not widen guards to excuse this conflict. A future separately allocated operation first needs a coherent use of existing profiler suspension/manual controls and proof of idle state before arming standalone timers. This is a preparation prerequisite, not a source optimization premise or authority for another launch.

## Costs and uncertainty

[Component analysis](component-analysis.json) retains137 startup cache scans: summed12.777ms wall/12.228ms threadCPU, median23.916us/20.459us. Startup47107rows/dropped0 includes37946metadata hooks and9024flush hooks, mostly inactive. At gallery, configure reset leaves7320prearm rows/dropped0 (6222inactive metadata,1098empty flush); cumulative scans205. The reset therefore prevents startup occupancy carrying into an arm. No active gallery candidate or reverse read was reached; startup/current inactive records cannot establish component dominance. No cap overwrite observed; prospective cap-hit would stop. Full cache scan history after startup through gallery is not retained across the intentional reset; cumulative counts are not a retained-memory or mesh identity proof.

Current active metadata/bounds/projection/query issue/collection/replay/cache activation costs, per-group read latencies/order/total/max wait, context work counts, native+candidate SOLID GPU and totalframe bracket remain missing. The raw record schema is ready but has no measured active records in this allocation. Timestamp/elapsed capability reporting is not completed C01 timing. Existing available asynchronous C01 timer was never configured; capability/epoch/error/disjoint semantics were not changed. Broad GpuTimers cannot isolate native early-depth. Heap775998680→834718936bytes is whole-JVM context, not retained cache/RSS/GPU residency. Full startup, construction/allocation, activation and memory costs are not zero or amortized away; no payback estimate.

Wall−threadCPU includes scheduling/driver blocking, not GPU time; inclusive scopes overlap and cannot be summed. Instrumented proxy/sample/timer queries perturb execution. No cross-arm subtraction/netgain, CPUwait-as-GPUtime, primitive-percent-as-time, independent-frame or clean lean comparison claim. Historical71.805% primitive suppression,7424observerpairs0falsehidden,8queries/frame and native26.3→27.9ms drift remain historical until rejoined. No next optimization premise selected; park the precise missing data.

## Restoration and retained storage

[FINAL-RESTORATION](FINAL-RESTORATION.json) passed: failed-restored operation, configuration_restored/release_verified true; all exact captured PID/birth/argv identities absent, empty fresh client census, lane/save locks free, canonical full world/config/options unchanged. One failfast dependent finalizer checked [pre-reset proof](pre-reset-verified.json), then common checked checkout, then [full post-reset maps/locks](after-reset.json). No old-inode recovery or custody transfer. The reused finalizer's initial inventory label said R2; storage-steward corrects this reporting label to R3 without changing operational receipts.

[Storage-steward](storage-steward.json) retains about38MB useful preparation/failure/restoration evidence,153MB shared reusable build output and70MB managed slot, plus preexisting shared dependency caches and daemon. Unique uncertain backups remain outside the pool. No substantial disposable artifacts, worktrees, downloads or servers were created; no owned live runtime remains. Small own bytecode is removed if present, measured free-byte delta recorded with concurrency caveat. All shared dirty source/results/caches preserved; no STATUS/goal/G05/G04 edits, subagents, commits, pushes, paid resources, PC/C02 or default promotion. Root owns fresh independent reviews and actual debate.

# G04 R2: finite Asahi material survey, no executed class0 observed

G04 remains **OPEN/default Off**, all11 OPEN/0 closed. One actual untimed Asahi operation completed. Six prospectively frozen existing authored views × three readbacks produced **zero code1/class0 pixels in both banks for all18 observations**. Positive code3/glass and code4/water counts demonstrate a working observer on real translucent draws. This is finite visible-material coverage, not a proof that the gallery/world contains no class0 or that G04 is exhausted. No candidate timing, gain, payback or affected-quality qualification follows.

Only this `g04-r2` directory was changed. No public guard widening, Mac spoof, vertex skip, G05 Java edits, STATUS/goal edits, subagents, commits, pushes, PC work, personal settings, installation or default promotion. Concurrent G05 desk work and shared Gradle/cache inputs were preserved. Old parent remained interrupted.

## Native classmap and real pass route

[Native classmap](native-classmap.json) joins exact pinned MakeUp9.5g to cached MC1.21.1/NeoForge21.1.253 source. [Extracted loader source](ItemBlockRenderTypes.java), [Sodium material bytecode](sodium-route.javap), [Iris routing](iris-route.javap), [Iris program mapping](iris-programs.javap) and [pass enum](iris-pass.javap) preserve the route. Sodium maps translucent RenderType to TRANSLUCENT; Iris maps that terrain pass to ProgramId.Water, resolving the existing world0 `gbuffers_water` shader. Native wrappers define GBUFFER_WATER/WATER_F. The native vertex initializes blockType=0, assigns3 for mc_Entity.x=10008 and2 for10079; primitive-constant IDs distinguish those classes. An entity, cutout block or merely transparent texture does not thereby enter this terrain pass.

| Native geometry/material | Native result in this route |
|---|---|
| Water/bubble-column fluid geometry mapped10008 | class3, native water/refraction/reflection path |
| All sixteen stained-glass blocks and panes, ice, slime, tinted glass mapped10079 | class2, native glass/reflection path |
| Honey block and frosted ice | No10008/10079 mapping; class0 if submitted through this translucent terrain route |
| Nether portal block terrain surface, mapped10091 | class0 in this water vertex; actual visible submission/scene coverage still required |
| Clear glass and clear glass pane | Loader cutout/cutout-mipped, so appearance alone is no proof of this class0 route |
| Leaves, opaque ordinary gallery blocks, block entities | Their own pass/renderer; no inferred water-fragment class0 coverage |

This is a vanilla loader/pack source survey, not a universal list for arbitrary modded render types or resource overrides. Complete mapped translucent block rows are retained in the JSON. Current runtime selected only vanilla/mod resources, no DH/Voxy or PBR pack. Neither honey, frosted ice nor portal was inferred from a screenshot. No world blocks were changed.

The exact public branch is only `blockType == 0.0`, after native dither initialization and before water-normal construction. It duplicates the native ordinary texture/tint, shadow (including colored shadow), illumination and final fog/darkness/output suffix, then returns. It avoids otherwise unconsumed wave normals, surface normal, eye/fresnel, reflection vector, sky reflection and conditional cloud setup. Water/glass and unsupported configurations continue through native bodies. The optional vertex omission remains disabled. Native writebuffers clamps RGBA and writes output0 to colortex1 (`DRAWBUFFERS:1`); finalcolor still reads native fog gaux4 where applicable. Native shadow, material texture and final fog inputs remain. Source omissions/counts are not physical sampler transactions or a statement about what the driver already eliminates.

## Observer, source/build/history and runtime joins

[Prepared observer](observer.json) uses the existing finite RT8 histogram builder/readback, adding only a private default0 option and Linux exact-version guard. The opt-in sidecar enables it only in this operation; real host/stack identity was checked before selection. The shader OS macro alone is not a hardware certificate. No MC_OS_MAC was injected. Native vertex and native RGBA/output include are byte-identical; the observer adds a separate R16F target8 with `DRAWBUFFERS:18`, clear0 and blending off. Code1 means class0,3 glass,4 water,257 unexpected/unordered. Generic eligible_pixels counts every nonzero class and must not be substituted for code1. Both banks, dimensions, full histograms and pixel-store/FBO restoration are retained. These are last visible raster fragments after depth testing, not overdraw counts or lean branch executions.

[Prelaunch freeze](prelaunch-seal.json), [source checks](source-checks.json), [actual JVM properties](actual-jvm.json), [source/build/output join](source-build-output-joins.json) and [runtime](survey/summary.json) identify actual inputs and selected sources. Existing source-consistent compiled outputs were reused; no build or broad test suite was needed. Proven neoForge.runs.configureEach forwarding and static preflight preceded launch; actual properties were persisted before observer assertions. fragmentWorkProbe/cloudSamplerProbe are true; cameraQuality/pixelHistoryCapture/physicalResolution and hierarchy probe flags are absent. No blank forbidden properties were supplied. Private controls were staged transactionally but not selected because all views were zero.

Native initial/return exported stage maps are exactly equal. Observer exported water source contains the actual histogram expression and output layout. Selection is joined to positive glass/water readbacks. [History/current joins](history-current-joins.json) finds all nine prior G04 public pins unchanged, retaining source ancestry rather than transporting historical runtime qualification. r33/r35's18 observations of zero class0, historical Mac honey positive/reversal failure, and prior native-null4.68% median spread/+1.35% drift remain separate historical evidence. The assistant-selected1% prior screen is not a universal/user gate. No unchanged null study was repeated. Fastpath repaired quick-path and G05 R3 release/reset receipts were read and independently followed by actual fresh process/lock/full-map checks in [baseline](baseline.json).

|0|0/0|2660–2665|1741–1752|
|1|0/0|5700–5774|9–10|
|2|0/0|0|261546|
|3|0/0|0|2035637–2036249|
|4|0/0|64921–65051|3592–3714|
|6|0/0|64888–65064|3589–3696|

[Affected-quality disposition](affected-quality.json) records **branch-active ordinary still/motion and same-fragment native/candidate scalar/output evidence missing**. Conditional lean native/false/active sequence was not entered. No motion images or invented same-frame comparison. No existing trustworthy G04 same-frame scalar route was identified; no generic witness framework was added.

## Fixture refusal and next discriminator

[Fixture admission](fixture-admission.json) records missing exact historical fixture receipt and implementation/JAR caller inputs. Bounded searches found historical callers/results, but the callers point at absent implementation paths. Therefore exact prospective coordinates, native-class fixture source, transactional restoration and full-world backup provenance could not be established. No fixture was added; no canonical edit, new worldgen or unsafe backup/copy occurred. This is a missing material avenue, **not exhaustion or an external blocker claim**.

[Budget](operation-budget.json):900s science +300s recovery under1200s watchdog, one operation/no retry/no hot windows. [Final restoration](FINAL-RESTORATION.json), [pre-reset verification](pre-reset-verified.json), [backup classifications](backup-manifest.json), [post-reset full maps/locks](after-reset.json), [storage](storage-steward.json). One fail-fast finalizer required terminal restored/released operation, exact PID birth/argv absence, empty client census, free lane/save locks, unchanged full canonical world/config/options, exact original pool config/options plus individually preserved new backups, before common checkout. Checked checkout succeeded; post-reset pool full world/config/options equal canonical. Ordinary operation save writes were reset by managed checkout; no fixture world mutation existed. All newly generated backups were individually classified and retained outside pool, including uncertain bytes. No old-inode recovery after reset. All owned controller/supervisor/launcher/client processes are absent; no custody transferred. Shared daemon/caches/builds and all preexisting dirty work retained.

# G05 R3: private producer control and complete R2 cost cohort

**Completed: the private producer-absent native control qualifies on the exact assigned Asahi tuple; one complete frozen 16-window R2 cost cohort shows no gain. Recommend parking this tested configuration pending new independent cost reviews. Broad G05 and all11 remain OPEN; zero closed.** No algorithm redesign, default promotion, commit, push, paid resource, PC/C02 work, subdelegation or STATUS/goal edit occurred.

Active total-frame cost was **7.8575% higher** than producer-free native, using the prospectively frozen equal-pair mean log(wall/completedframes). The exact two-sided sharp-null randomization p is **2/68 = 0.029412**. Pose2 cost was +4.7782%, pose3 +11.0273%; all eight pairs, both order groups and both chronological halves favor native. This is a measured adverse comparison on these two private scenes, not inference from expression counts. It does not establish universal loss, equivalence, pass-level GPU causality or broad hierarchy exhaustion. No replacement, suffix, removed arm or posthoc drift exclusion was used.

The [analysis](analysis.json) retains every pair/window, mean/median/p95/p99, native anchors, activation durations and supplementary precision. Native mean frame cost rose 6.316% at pose2 and 6.439% at pose3 from first to last native observation. That drift remains visible. Randomization inference assumes no residual arm carryover after settling; conditioning is not plateau proof. As an explicitly post-acquisition sensitivity description, an independent-normal-pair t interval gives +4.824% to +10.979%; it is not a frozen primary test, a randomization interval or a cure for drift/carryover. Pair effects range +3.173% to +14.125%. No reliable universal loss or equivalence claim follows.

## Private control change and qualification

[Owned changes](owned-changes.patch) show only the two source files changed against their actual dirty pre-edit bytes, retained under source-before. `shaderlod.dev.depthHierarchyCostAsahiR3` is explicit and absent by default. Absent opt-in preserves the previous producer-enable behavior. Opted-in sessions start disabled. The copied-depth gate precedes qualification/state capture/constructor/GL work; binding has the same gate and retains failure refusal. The private extent check refuses construction outside2560x1600. No native sampler, ray, march, repair, quantizer or archive guard was relaxed.

The new benchmark transaction runs on the render thread, rejects recording/motion/detailed timers, and requires the existing exact private lower-only/API/OS/arch/GPU/driver/loader/archive/options admission. Disable first prevents production, unbinds, disposes exactly the owned GL objects, clears copy/frame/owner/extents and binding fields, and preserves historical build/allocation/permission counters and failure refusals. Enable performs that same invalidation then only re-arms; the callback receipt is empty. Only a new authentic copy subsequently constructs and permits consumption. Ordinary pipeline destruction also invalidates these current fields. Historical last-draw binding fields are explicitly labeled; idle uniform status reads the actual linked program and is zero after unbind.

[31 actual receipt assertions](control-tests.json), [control body](body.py), [control operation](control/operation.json) and [control summary](control/summary.json) retain:

- Disabled native has zero owned resources and no build/allocation/positive-permission delta. Disabled active archive likewise does not construct.
- Each enable acknowledgment is empty; subsequent fresh active has a real owned copy, constructed resources and positive admitted draw count. Actual production readback checked260 tiles with zero mismatches.
- Disable clears current state. Reload while disabled stays empty. Re-enable after reload constructs fresh state.
- Forcedfalse retains producer and binding, increments false-permission counts, and admits no further positive permissions through native return. Every observed idle actual permission is zero.
- Native return remains producer-free with zero allocation/build delta. Both operations terminate restored/released.

These are exact-tuple private control tests, not public Apply/Quality/Cancel/failed-Apply/mismatch qualification. Recording/motion refusal and unknown/mismatched source/API/archive behavior are source-enforced; they were not exhaustively fault-injected at runtime. No permission was widened to make qualification pass. Five focused conservative-lower tests passed in [focused-tests.log](focused-tests.log); no broad suite, glslang or NumPy installation ran. Two offline current-source producer builds passed ([build.log](build.log), [build-final.log](build-final.log)).

## Inputs and source identity

[Source/build/archive/API joins](source-build-archive-joins.json), [prospective seal](prelaunch-seal.json), [actual JVM/argfiles](actual-jvm.json), [control JVM](control-actual-jvm.json) and [full build receipt](study/build-binding.json) identify actual source and compiled outputs, mixins, Iris/Sodium and the unchanged R2 lean archives. Effective properties were persisted before assertions. Private R50/parallel/lowerR2/costR3 flags are present; cameraQuality/pixelHistoryCapture/physicalResolution are absent, including blank properties. The configureEach forwarding hook was checked before launch. Probe/witness properties were not enabled for the cost study.

Actual tuple: Apple M1 G13G B1, Linux aarch64, Mesa25.1.0-asahi20250221 GL4.6, MC1.21.1/NF21.1.253/Iris1.8.12-local/Sodium0.6.13; JDK21.0.6.0.7-6.fc42-r1. MakeUp9.5g native100/AA2, Overworld/noDH/noVOXY,2560x1600/RD12/focused fullscreen/VSyncOff, vanilla+mod resources, day6000. Pose2=(.5,71,82.5,yaw0,pitch9); pose3=(.5,66,117.5,yaw0,pitch-3). All before/after states were checked against these inputs. The managed slot used the unchanged authored world; no copies outside run_storage or world generation occurred.

Actual native/active/false linked source dumps are retained in control and joined in the source receipt. The R2 lower-only Q and four4/4/4/2 reductions are unchanged. [R2 proof/store/trace/quality](../g05-r2/REPORT.md) remains the prior scoped evidence:106191 texels, actual trace zero observed mismatch and bounded still/sparse-motion acceptance. This pass does not expand that quality result or claim new continuous quality, DH/PBR, other loaders/hardware or public support. The parent amendment and original R2 snapshots were preserved.

## Frozen acquisition and costs

[Protocol](protocol.json) predates observations. The existing G07/G09 machinery drew uniformly from68 globally balanced orders with both orders represented per view; assignment index3 was selected. Analysis source is pinned and reused exactly for the primary. Eight pairs/two views, all16 valid windows, wall durations60.254–60.653s, no invalid/removed window. [Raw rows](study/rows.json) join per-window result.json/before.json/after.json/guard.json and raw frame samples; telemetry, load averages and CPU/GC observations remain in [summary](study/summary.json). Sensor values are context, never timing substitution. [Analysis sanity](analysis-sanity.json) passed null/known-effect/invalid-row cases.

There was600.033s genuinely producer-free native conditioning;30s common producer-free native before each pair;45s settling per arm. Activation switches used only the validated idle transaction outside recording. Forcedfalse prewarm was15s outside primary. Native is authentic archive/options with no producer; active pays all constructor draws/ALU/CPU/state, memory, guards, binding, consumer and per-draw history counters. The mod remains installed/Off in both. Minimal total-frame collection, no-op hierarchy mixin wrappers/property checks and ordinary mod overhead remain common; this is not mod-absent N or a tax-free whole-mod baseline. Nothing was subtracted using false.

The prospective conservative schedule totals4380s within4800s science,600s recovery and5400s watchdog. Startup/stage/prewarm600 + conditioning600 + pair preparation240 + settling720 + windows960 + switches/checks960 + final return300 =4380. Actual hot operation total3041.153s, including16.804s preparation/startup,39.206s world/initial warmup and42.513s restoration/release. The control operation took114.240s within1500s science+300s recovery/1800s watchdog. Both ran once, without runtime replacement/retry. Static preflight initially rejected the quick caller's default30s/1800s bounds; the same report-local60s/5400s adaptation already used by G07 was applied and passed before hot launch, preserving the frozen cohort. No source/build/tests/encoders or ancillary analysis ran during hot acquisition.

Measured full private selection/control/reload/readiness averages: native8.268s, active8.841s. Every individual duration is retained. The active duration includes invalidation, pack selection/reload, enable, fresh creation and readiness polling. Startup/build logs and stage receipts are retained, but shader compiler time, first-allocation GPU time and small archive-staging time were **not independently clocked**; bundled reload is not labeled compiler time. No public Apply cost is claimed. No new pack generation was needed. Resident scratch logical size remains1088000B; actual memory residency/transactions are not measured. Illustrative300/1800/7200s horizons cannot produce payback without steady benefit; measured payback is null. Untimed false cannot attribute the adverse effect between producer and consumer. The borrowed per60s charged estimator is descriptive only and is not the decision gate.

## Restoration and storage

Fresh pre-ownership checks independently matched G10's postreset full maps and verified all old owned identities absent; see [baseline](baseline.json). Installed p-stack runtime advertises observation mode; status still refuses on missing auth.key. No invented grant, broker repair or unrelated process stop occurred. Existing lane/save locks, PID/birth/argv supervision, finite watchdogs and storage limits remained in force. The preexisting Gradle daemon/caches were preserved.

[FINAL-RESTORATION](FINAL-RESTORATION.json) links terminal operation evidence, exact owned process absence, empty client census and free lane/save locks. Full canonical world/config/options maps remained unchanged. Every newly generated config backup was individually classified and byte-preserved outside the pool in [manifest](backup-manifest.json). All pre-reset assertions passed in one failfast Python process before checked common checkout; full postreset world/config/options maps and locks passed. Control and hot restoration proofs are both retained. No recovery touched a replaced old inode. There is no live process custody transfer.

[Storage disposition](storage-steward.json) retains about55MB useful raw/review evidence,152.6MB shared reusable build outputs and69.9MB protected reusable slot. No substantial disposable task artifact remained; no uncertain data/shared cache was deleted. Filesystem free space remains about127.7GB decimal; actual before/after bytes and concurrency caveat are in the receipt. Large artifacts/raw logs remain outside Git.

[Machine decision](DECISION.json) separates implemented preparation/control, prior bounded quality, complete cost, scoped parking recommendation and broad closure. New Astra high/Sol xhigh independent COST reviews and actual peer debate remain root-owned and unperformed here. No peer acceptance is claimed. A different hierarchy design remains a separately justified future question; no automatic rerun or broad implementation work follows this handback.
